constants.london_price_unit: Tickers ending in .L are quoted in pence (GBX) on the chart, including when the chart currency field says GBP. Statement amounts are in major currency units, then multiplied by 100 after conversion into pounds.

implausible_trailing_pe.formula: signal close in major units / latest EPS, both in the statement currency
implausible_trailing_pe.purpose: unit or currency error guard, not a valuation view
implausible_trailing_pe.skipped_when: latest EPS is missing or not positive

constants.scoring_population: Primary episodes with a range that are mature or closed. Other columns are stored and are not pooled into the primary buckets, because they are the same entry walked under a different exit.
constants.point_in_time: Statement years after the signal year are dropped (the decline gate's year rule). A financials file is used only when fetched_at is on or before the signal session; a later fetched_at is replaced by the last git blob of that file on or before the session when one exists. Snapshot currency uses the same git rule, because the snapshot has no fetched_at. SEC currency uses a row whose first_filed is on or before the session, and only when the file's fetched_at is too. The entry price is the chart close dated on the signal session. Recovery uses chart closes after the signal session and up to the exit session. FX is the committed macro history, not a live spot.

fx.point_in_time: Each rate's date is the marker as_of, not the snapshot file name and not a live spot. The converter uses the latest as_of on or before the episode date. fetch_fx_rates is not called.
